answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may vote on trades, with stake weighted rather than raw account count. If an operator splits one wallet across a thousand aliases, those aliases still control only the same locked stake; they do not create a louder echo or turn the tide. To sway a decision, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital and risking slashing if proven to be colluding. The harbor is not invulnerable, but fake names alone buy no influence.
